newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court dismisses appeal from Viho against Commission.
newsitem.headline: Court dismisses appeal from Viho against Commission.

text.p: The European Court of Justice dismissed on Thursday an appeal from Dutch office equipment supplier Viho Europe against Parker Pen's pricing and distribution policies in the European Union.

In January 1995, the Court of First Instance (CFI) ruled against Viho. The CFI held that Parker subsidiaries were all part of one economic unit which could coordinate on pricing and distribution policies without infringing competiton rules.
Viho appealed that judgment to the Court of Justice, but again their pleas were rejected and Viho was ordered to pay costs.
The court found Viho failed to adequately support its appeal with alleged flaws in the CFI's judgment and with legal arguments to support their application.
Parker Pen was fined 700,000 Ecus by the Commission in 1992 for operating an exclusive export network to Germany, and the court subsequently reduced the fine to 400,000 Ecus.
(Court translates into English. Original language of the case: German)
"Competition - Groups of companies - Article 85(1) of the Treaty"
appeal against the judgment of the Court of First Instance of the European Communities in Case T-102/92 Viho v Commission (1995) ECR II-17, seeking to have that judgment set aside,
